title: How fossils form
keyIdea: A fossil is the shape of something that once lived, trapped inside rock. First the plant or animal dies and gets buried in mud or sand. More layers pile on. Over millions of years that soft mud hardens into rock, and the shape stays inside. Digging later can reveal a shell, bone, leaf imprint or footprint fossil.

kid: A fossil is a shape in rock. It came from a plant or animal that lived a very long time ago.
First the plant or animal dies and gets covered by soft mud or sand. More mud piles on, layer after layer.
Over millions of years the mud is squashed and turns into hard rock. The shape stays trapped inside.
When we dig the rock, we can find that shape: a shell, a bone, a leaf mark or a footprint. That shape is the fossil.
adult: Year 3 science in England asks children to describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock (NC Y3 Rocks). Keep the story short: die and bury, sediment layers, deep time, rock, then the preserved shape.

Words to use: fossil, sediment, mud, sand, layers, rock, millions of years, shell, bone, imprint, footprint. A common mistake is thinking any old stone is a fossil, or that plastic toys and metal coins count. Fossils come from living things. Another slip is thinking fossils form in days or weeks; the rock step takes millions of years.
In the lab your child buries a shell, piles sediment layers, waits for rock, digs the fossil out, then sorts finds into fossil or not.

familyTip: Look at a fossil picture book or a museum photo together. Ask 'What living thing left this shape?' and 'What covered it so it did not rot away?' On a beach, talk about shells sinking into wet sand as a tiny first step of the same idea.

visual.caption: Fossil or not? Drag each find, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: bury a shell, pile sediment layers, wait millions of years for rock, dig out the fossil, and sort fossil vs not.

choices: a shape of a living thing trapped in rock
any old stone on the path
a plastic model of a dinosaur
practice.hint: Think about something that once lived, then got trapped for a very long time.
practice.explain: A fossil is the shape left by a living thing that was buried and turned into rock over a very long time.

practice.prompt: What must happen first for a fossil to form?
choices: the living thing is buried in mud or sand
the bones are left in bright sun
practice.hint: Burial protects the shape so it is not eaten or washed away.
practice.explain: Burial under mud or sand is the first step. Without it, the body usually rots or is scattered.

practice.prompt: How long does soft mud usually take to become hard fossil rock?
practice.hint: Fossil rock forms on a deep-time scale, not a school-week scale.
practice.explain: Turning sediment into rock takes millions of years of pressure and time.

practice.prompt: A fossil dig finds {n} shell fossils and 2 bone fossils. How many fossils in total?
practice.hint: Add the shell fossils to the bone fossils.

practice.prompt: Four sediment layers pile up each year for {n} years in a model. How many layers is that?
practice.hint: Four layers every year, for that many years.
practice.explain: 4 layers × {n} years = {=4*n} layers in the model.

pool.prompt: Which of these can become a fossil?
choices: a leaf that was buried in mud
pool.hint: Fossils come from things that once lived.
pool.explain: A leaf is from a living plant. Plastic and glass are not from living things.

pool.hint: Think of what rivers and seas drop on the bottom.
pool.explain: Sediment is natural mud, sand and silt that settle in water or wind.

pool.prompt: A footprint in rock can be a fossil because…
choices: an animal once stood there and the print was buried
someone drew it yesterday with chalk
it is made of shiny metal
pool.hint: The print must come from a real living animal long ago.
pool.explain: Trace fossils like footprints form when an animal presses into soft ground that later turns to rock.

pool.prompt: Why is a plastic dinosaur toy not a fossil?
choices: it was never a living thing trapped in rock
pool.hint: Ask: did this toy once live, die and get buried for millions of years?
pool.explain: Toys are made by people. Fossils form from real living things trapped in rock.

pool.prompt: After burial, what piles on top over time?
choices: more layers of mud and sand
pool.hint: Year after year, more sediment settles.
pool.explain: More sediment layers build up and squash what is underneath.

pool.prompt: When you dig a fossil carefully, you are trying to…
choices: keep the shape inside the rock whole
pool.hint: Fossils can crack if you hit them hard.
pool.explain: Careful digging protects the fragile fossil shape preserved in the rock.

pool.prompt: A tray shows {n} fossil shells and you add 3 more. How many shells now?
A model uses {n} layers of sand. Each layer is 2 cm thick. How many cm tall is the stack?
pool.hint: Multiply the number of layers by 2 cm.
